items.title: FOMC statement, 16 Sep 2026
items.headline: US Fed raises its key interest rate by 1/4 point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent
items.decision: The Fed's rate-setting committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, and is continuing to maintain ample reserves in the banking system.
items.summary: The US Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate by 1/4 percentage point, and all 12 voting members agreed. It describes economic activity as expanding at a solid pace, but says inflation remains elevated. It says the rate rise will support a timelier return to its 2 percent inflation goal.
points: The target range for the federal funds rate was raised by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
The vote was 12-0 in favour of the statement.
Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace and domestic spending has been resilient.
Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.
Inflation remains elevated, and the Committee says it will deliver price stability.
watch: Uncertainty remains elevated, in part because of geopolitical developments.
Inflation is still elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal.
The statement says the action is meant to support a timelier return of inflation to 2 percent.

items.title: MPC decision, 5 Aug 2026
items.headline: RBI keeps repo rate at 5.25% and neutral stance; says it needs more clarity on inflation
items.decision: The MPC voted unanimously to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent and to continue with the neutral stance.
items.summary: The RBI left rates unchanged, saying the outlook is hazy because of the monsoon, El Niño, West Asia conflict and global trade policy. Inflation rose to 4.4 per cent in June and is projected to peak in Q3 of 2026-27, mainly because of food and fuel. Growth is described as resilient but expected to be lower in 2026-27.
points: Repo rate stays at 5.25 per cent; SDF rate at 5.00 per cent; MSF rate and Bank Rate at 5.50 per cent.
CPI inflation rose to 4.4 per cent in June 2026 after 16 months below target, but was 30 bps lower than projected for Q1. Core inflation stayed at 3.9 per cent.
The MPC says higher inflation is mainly from food and fuel, with little sign so far of price pressures becoming broad-based.
Real GDP growth for 2026-27 is projected at 6.7 per cent, with risks described as evenly balanced. Domestic demand, manufacturing, services and exports were described as resilient in Q1.
The MPC says greater clarity is needed on inflation's path and composition before taking any policy action.
watch: The south-west monsoon and El Niño, which the statement says remain a risk to food prices, agriculture and rural demand.
West Asia conflict and volatile oil prices, which blur the near-term outlook and could feed into food, fuel and other input prices.
Whether underlying inflation normalises from its benign levels, and whether higher food and fuel prices turn into broad-based inflation.

items.title: FOMC statement, 29 Jul 2026
items.headline: Fed holds rates at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent; three members wanted a hike
items.decision: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, in a 9-3 vote.
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its key interest rate unchanged. It describes economic activity as expanding at a solid pace, while inflation remains elevated relative to its 2 percent goal. Three members voted against the decision because they preferred a 1/4 percentage point rate increase.
points: The target range for the federal funds rate stays at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent.
The vote was 9-3; Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari and Lorie K. Logan preferred to raise the range by 1/4 percentage point.
Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace, with strong productivity growth and capital investment.
Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.
Inflation remains elevated relative to the 2 percent goal, partly due to supply shocks that have pushed up prices in some sectors, including energy.
watch: Elevated uncertainty, which the statement says owes in part to the conflict in the Middle East.
Inflation, which remains elevated relative to the 2 percent goal, partly reflecting supply shocks including in energy.
The statement says the Committee will deliver price stability.
